source: The platforms' pricing pages, read 2026-10-11 for the smallest paid size of each part: heroku.com/pricing and devcenter.heroku.com (Basic dyno $7, Essential-0 Postgres $5, Mini Key-Value Store $3, Scheduler jobs on one-off Basic dynos); fly.io/docs/about/pricing (shared-cpu-1x with 512 MB $3.32 a month, volumes $0.15 a GB, egress $0.02 a GB in Europe and North America); docs.railway.com/pricing ($20 a vCPU and $10 a GB of RAM a month, volumes $0.15 a GB, egress $0.05 a GB; Railway bills use, so a service is taken as 0.1 vCPU on average and 0.5 GB of RAM); render.com (Starter instance $7, Postgres Basic-256mb $6 with 1 GB of storage at $0.30, Key Value Starter $10, disks $0.25 a GB; the pricing page renders in the browser, so these four are as Render published them in 2026 and were not re-read). The audit does not read a plan's size yet, so every part is priced at the smallest paid size; the bill answer replaces all of it.

scheduled.size: one-off Basic dyno runs, a few minutes a day

diskGb.size: no disk: the dyno's files are lost on restart

Heroku.sleep: Heroku sleeps only Eco dynos; this app runs on paid dynos, which run every hour.

scheduled.size: a cron job, Starter, billed by the minute

Render.sleep: Render spins down only free instances; this app runs on a paid instance, which runs every hour.

scheduled.size: a scheduled Machine, a few minutes a day

db.size: a Postgres Machine, shared-cpu-1x with 512 MB

cache.size: a Redis Machine, shared-cpu-1x with 512 MB

Fly.io.sleep: Fly.io can stop idle machines (auto_stop_machines); fly.toml keeps them running, so they run every hour.

process.size: a service at 0.1 vCPU and 0.5 GB on average

scheduled.size: a cron service, a few minutes a day

db.size: a Postgres service at 0.1 vCPU, 0.5 GB and a 1 GB volume

cache.size: a Redis service at 0.1 vCPU and 0.5 GB

Railway.sleep: Railway can put a service to sleep when it has no traffic and wake it on the next request; that setting is off unless a service turns it on, so these processes run every hour.
